facts.text: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis.
Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any excipients in the formulation.

Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis may occur; risk factors include age ≥ 65 years, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment, concomitant use of interacting drugs, and higher atorvastatin doses. Discontinue if markedly elevated CK or clinical myopathy is diagnosed.
Immune‑mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) has been reported; discontinue atorvastatin if IMNM is suspected.

Hepatic dysfunction: transient elevations in transaminases are common; persistent >3× ULN occurs in ~0.7 % of patients. Monitor liver enzymes and discontinue if serious hepatic injury, hyperbilirubinemia, or jaundice develops.
Statins, including atorvastatin, may increase HbA1c and fasting glucose; lifestyle measures should be optimized.
In patients receiving 80 mg daily, there is an increased risk of hemorrhagic stroke after a recent hemorrhagic stroke (HR ≈ 1.68).

Renal impairment is a risk factor for myopathy; acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis has been reported. Temporarily discontinue atorvastatin in acute conditions with high risk of renal failure (e.g., sepsis, shock, major surgery).
facts.population: Patients with renal impairment or acute serious illness

facts.text: Patients ≥ 65 years have a higher incidence of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; dose selection should be cautious and patients monitored for muscle symptoms.
Adults: start 10 mg or 20 mg once daily; dose range 10 mg–80 mg daily. Patients needing >45 % LDL‑C reduction may start at 40 mg daily.
Pediatric patients ≥ 10 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH): start 10 mg once daily; dose range 10 mg–20 mg daily.
Pediatric patients ≥ 10 years with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH): start 10–20 mg once daily; dose range 10 mg–80 mg daily.
Take orally once daily with or without food; assess LDL‑C as early as 4 weeks after initiation and adjust dose as needed.
When co‑administered with cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, tipranavir + ritonavir, or glecaprevir + pibrentasvir, do not use atorvastatin (interaction not recommended).
With saquinavir + ritonavir, darunavir + ritonavir, fosamprenavir ± ritonavir, elbasvir + grazoprevir, or letermovir: do not exceed 20 mg daily.
With nelfinavir: do not exceed 40 mg daily.
With clarithromycin or itraconazole: do not exceed 20 mg daily.
CYP3A4 and transporter inhibitors (e.g., azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, many antivirals) increase atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk; dose limits or avoidance are required.
facts.population: All patients taking CYP3A4/transport inhibitor drugs

facts.text: Rifampin induces CYP3A4 and reduces atorvastatin exposure; administer simultaneously to mitigate interaction.
Grapefruit juice >1.2 L/day markedly raises atorvastatin levels; avoid large quantities.
Concomitant high‑dose niacin (>1 g/day), fibrates (except gemfibrozil), or colchicine increase myopathy risk; monitor closely if used together.
Atorvastatin increases plasma concentrations of norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol; consider when selecting oral contraceptives.
Atorvastatin raises digoxin levels; monitor digoxin concentrations and adjust as needed.
